truth_boundary.note: The mitochondrial model describes canonical neuronal mitochondrial anatomy. It is not microscopy, telemetry, or a reconstruction from a specific CL1 cell.

claims: The CL API is designed to interact with biological neural networks on CL1.
The API supports recording, stimulation, and real-time closed-loop workflows.
The SDK simulator is intended as a drop-in development environment for CL1 applications.
Cortical Labs describes living neurons cultured in nutrient solution across a silicon interface.
Cortical Labs describes a closed-loop environment linking software and neuronal activity.
The product page states the life-support environment is designed to maintain neurons for up to six months.
Cortical Cloud is described as remote deployment of code to CL1 biological neural networks.
The platform is described as monitoring neural health and performance.
The CL API paper describes sub-millisecond closed-loop interaction with biological neural networks.
It documents deterministic stimulation semantics, recording, and synchronization behavior.
Mitochondrial inner membranes form cristae that support oxidative phosphorylation.
ATP synthase oligomers and MICOS are major organizers of crista architecture.
Cristae are dynamic compartments central to ATP production, signaling, and mitochondrial homeostasis.
Cristae remodeling can alter cytochrome-c release, mtDNA exposure, and ROS signaling.

prohibited_inferences: Do not claim a specific CL1 neuron was imaged at mitochondrial resolution.
Do not infer ATP production, membrane potential, ROS, or mitochondrial health from CL1 spike data alone.
Do not equate GPT-Doug's software 'mitochondrial compute units' with biological ATP.
